question: If top AI models keep getting cheaper, what will make one choice better than another?
reflection: Lower prices can open strong AI to schools, small firms and public services that could not afford it before.

sources.subject: xAI Grok 4.6 Launch, DeepSeek V4-Pro GA, Claude Cowork Sync

one_line: Two new top-tier models arrived on the same day with sharply lower prices, a sign that frontier AI is turning into a commodity.

top_stories.title: Grok 4.6 competes on price
top_stories.what: xAI released Grok 4.6 for long, multi-step tasks, priced at well under half of a leading rival model per word processed.
top_stories.why: Price pressure makes it worth re-checking which model gives the best value for each project task.

top_stories.title: DeepSeek V4-Pro goes live with night discounts
top_stories.what: DeepSeek made its V4-Pro model generally available with a very long input limit and half-price rates outside peak hours.
top_stories.why: Scheduling large analysis jobs overnight could cut research costs noticeably.

top_stories.title: Browser assistant joins the main workspace
top_stories.what: Anthropic connected its Chrome browser assistant to the same sessions used on desktop and phone, while warning that browser agents can be tricked by hidden page instructions.
top_stories.why: Browser agents that use your logins need clear limits before they handle client or citizen data.

saudi_lens.text: Falling model prices lower the cost of Arabic AI services for Saudi agencies, though the cheapest model is not always the safest choice for sensitive data.

idea.title: Model value scorecard
idea.pitch: A simple quarterly scorecard that compares models on cost, accuracy in Arabic and data handling for a client's main tasks.
idea.first_step: Choose three typical tasks and run them on two cheaper models this week.

idea_kids.title: Smart shopper market
idea_kids.pitch: A pretend market where children compare price and quality of toy goods and explain why the cheapest is not always the best.
idea_kids.first_step: Make price tags and quality cards for ten pretend items.

terms.definition: The amount of text an AI model can read and keep in mind at one time.
Hidden instructions placed in content an AI reads, meant to make it do something its user did not want.
A hidden signal added to AI-made content so it can later be identified as AI-made.

Tools to strip watermarks weaken ways of spotting AI text.
Assistants that act in your browser with your logins.
